subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Pop, rock and music theatre styles

questions.q: What is the name for a short, catchy melodic or rhythmic pattern that is repeated throughout a pop or rock song?
questions.explain: A riff is a short, repeated musical idea that is central to much rock and pop music.

questions.q: The standard 12-bar blues progression is built from which three chords?
questions.explain: The 12-bar blues uses only the tonic (I), subdominant (IV) and dominant (V) chords.

questions.q: Which studio technique records separate layers of sound onto different tracks so they can be combined later?
questions.explain: Multitracking allows each instrument or voice to be recorded separately and then mixed together.

questions.q: What is the term for the most memorable, catchy part of a pop song designed to grab the listener?
questions.explain: The hook is the memorable musical phrase intended to catch and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: In a typical 4/4 rock groove, on which beats does the snare drum create the backbeat?
questions.explain: The backbeat places the strong snare accents on beats 2 and 4 of the bar.

questions.q: In music theatre, what is the term for a recurring musical theme associated with a particular character or idea?
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a short recurring theme linked to a character, place or idea in a dramatic work.

questions.q: Which guitar effect overdrives the signal to produce a gritty, aggressive tone often used in rock?
questions.explain: Distortion deliberately overdrives the amplifier signal to create a harsh, edgy guitar sound.

questions.q: What is the main role of the chorus in verse-chorus form?
options: It repeats with the same words and carries the main hook
It changes its words on every appearance
It always contains an improvised solo
questions.explain: The chorus usually returns unchanged and delivers the song's central, memorable message.

questions.q: Why is syncopation frequently used in popular music?
options: To place accents on off-beats and create rhythmic interest
To slow the tempo down gradually
To keep the rhythm strictly on the beat
To remove the percussion from the texture
questions.explain: Syncopation stresses weak or off beats, giving pop and rock rhythms their drive and interest.

questions.q: What does a sequencer allow a music producer to do?
options: Record, edit and play back MIDI data to control sounds
questions.explain: A sequencer captures and manipulates MIDI information, triggering synthesised or sampled sounds.

questions.q: Which description best fits a power ballad?
options: A slow, emotional song that builds to a big climax with the full band
A spoken-word rap over a beat
questions.explain: A power ballad begins gently and builds in dynamics and texture to a powerful climax.

questions.q: What is the function of a middle 8 (bridge) within a pop song?
options: To provide contrasting material that breaks up the verse and chorus
To state the main hook of the song
To open the song before the first verse
To fade the song out at the end
questions.explain: The middle 8 offers fresh, contrasting material before the final return of the chorus.

questions.q: What is the purpose of adding reverb to a recorded sound?
options: To add a sense of space and ambience to the sound
To raise the pitch by an octave
To shorten the length of each note
To convert the audio into MIDI data
questions.explain: Reverb simulates natural reflections, giving a recording a sense of acoustic space.

questions.q: What does it mean for a musical to be described as through-composed (sung-through)?
options: It has continuous music with little or no spoken dialogue
It uses only the 12-bar blues throughout
It contains no singing at all
It repeats a single song from start to finish
questions.explain: A sung-through musical sets the story to continuous music rather than alternating songs with spoken scenes.

questions.q: A song in C major follows a standard 12-bar blues. Which three chords would you expect to hear?
options: C, E flat and B flat
C, A minor and D minor
questions.explain: In C major the I, IV and V chords are C, F and G respectively.

questions.q: A producer wants a single vocalist to sound like a large backing choir. Which technique is most suitable?
options: Overdubbing and layering multiple vocal takes
Adding a wah-wah pedal to the vocal
Applying heavy distortion to the vocal
Slowing the overall tempo of the track
questions.explain: Recording the voice repeatedly and stacking the takes builds a thick, choir-like vocal texture.

questions.q: In a rock track the drummer plays the snare firmly on beats 2 and 4 of every bar. What is this groove called?
questions.explain: Accenting beats 2 and 4 on the snare creates the driving backbeat typical of rock and pop.

questions.q: In a stage musical, a lone character sings a number expressing their personal feelings directly to the audience. This is best described as which type of number?
questions.explain: A solo character song lets one character reveal their thoughts and emotions to the audience.
